09:30 Local Time, 04:00 GMT, 09:30 IST: It was an evenly poised opening day in the Colombo Test, with India reaching 300 runs while Sri Lanka reduced them to five wickets by Stumps. Devdutt Padikkal continued his excellent run, bringing up his second century of the series, while Yashasvi Jaiswal, Shubman Gill and Ravindra Jadeja also made valuable contributions. For Sri Lanka, Asitha Fernando was the standout bowler, claiming three crucial wickets and leading the attack effectively. However, his heated exchange with Jaiswal was an unfortunate moment and took some shine off an otherwise competitive day.

The pitch offered some assistance to the pacers, but considering the history of this venue, batting conditions could improve on Day 2. Sri Lanka will be hoping to make the most of it and build a substantial total when their turn comes. For now, the big question is how many more runs India can add to their overnight score. Can they push past the 400-run mark? Day 2 should provide the answer.

Pitch report [Russel Arnold]: The pitch, it's still a batting day, I would think. India in a very good position. And when I look at this, there's not much that I can report about. But of course, wear and tear will kick in. Now what's different in this pitch from the Galle pitch? Initially, comparing the first day's play, there's more bounce here on offer than in Galle. Now that's considerable, even if you say four centimeters. Now we look at where the bowlers bowled yesterday. They have used very different lengths. The effective length has been the good length. If you look at the point the fast bowlers have bowled, all four wickets are there, but it's been effective because they've used the shorter one and the extra bounce. So that means this pitch is quickening up, and hence when the wear and tear comes in, it will be tougher to bat. So Sri Lanka need to somehow get the wickets early. If not, they will not get a lease of a good pitch on offer to score runs.
Rishabh Pant, who picked up an injury yesterday evening, is available to bat and, in fact, never left the ground. Harsha Bhogle confirmed on air that Pant was ready to bat even last evening.

Saransh Jain - (on getting the debut cap) I had mixed emotions. When I received the cap, I was happy and excited, resulting in mixed feelings. When I started playing cricket, of course, every player’s dream is to represent India. And even if I hadn’t received the cap yesterday, I definitely believed that I would represent India in the next one or two years. (on his preference for red-ball cricket) I feel that red-ball cricket requires a little more skill, you could say, and it requires more time. 12:02 Local Time, 06:32 GMT, 12:02 IST: 119 for 1 in the session and it's fair to say that India are slowly seizing control over this Test. They lost Saransh Jain early in the session, but Rishabh Pant resumed his innings. He braved blows from Asitha Fernando and Lahiru Kumara, but he didn't flinch and took the attack back to the opponents. Quite a subdued innings by his normal standard, but he stuck to his task and got India past the 400-run mark. At the other end was a fluent Dhruv Jurel - the Indian number 7 is slowly getting into the Test mold - solid defence combined with attractive shots - he too went past his half-century and this 112-run unbroken stand has pushed the visitors ahead in the Test. The Sri Lankan pacers bowled with a lot of heart, but the spinners have been ineffective, despite the pitch starting to offer them more in terms of turn and bounce. We'll be back at 12:40 pm for the post-lunch session..
-- This is the second time India have had a century stand for seventh wicket or lower in Tests in Sri Lanka, after 104 between Cheteshwar Pujara and Amit Mishra at the same venue in 2015.
-- This is the 11th time that a team has posted 400-plus in the first innings of a Test at this venue. Of the previous 10, six resulted in wins while four ended in draws.
